title: Rev. Paul Cuffee
summary: Rev. Paul Cuffee (1757-1812) was a Native Congregational minister born into Shinnecock and Unkechaug-connected family networks in Brookhaven. After early life in Wading River, he was ordained at Poospatuck in 1790 and traveled a preaching circuit that connected Wading River, Poospatuck, Islip, Canoe Place, Shinnecock, and Montauk. His life reflects Native-led ministry, kinship, travel, and community continuity across Long Island during a period of colonial pressure and change.
content:
Rev. Paul Cuffee (March 4, 1757–March 7, 1812) was a Native Congregational minister born into Shinnecock and Unkechaug-connected family networks in Brookhaven. Ordained at Poospatuck in 1790, he traveled a preaching circuit connecting Wading River, Poospatuck, Islip, Canoe Place, Shinnecock, and Montauk.

Historical Context

Cuffee was born in Brookhaven to Peter Cuffee and Jane Peters Cuffee. Sources describe his father as Shinnecock/Unkechaug-connected and his mother as Shinnecock.13

As a young person, he was bound out for farm labor in Wading River before entering the ministry.13

In 1790, the Connecticut Strict Congregational Convention ordained Cuffee at Poospatuck. His preaching circuit connected Wading River, Poospatuck, Islip, Canoe Place, Shinnecock, and Montauk.12

Cuffee is also associated with June Meeting. Stone describes his role carefully: translating older spring gathering rites into a Christian festival may have been his idea, but the gathering itself had deeper Native roots and should not be described as something he simply invented.4

He died on March 7, 1812 and was buried at the Native burial ground at Canoe Place in what is now Hampton Bays. The exact grave location is not identified.3

References

  1. John A. Strong, The Unkechaug Indians of Eastern Long Island: A History, p. 149.
  2. Rev. Earnest Edward Eells, Indian Missions on Long Island.
  3. Brewster-Walker, The Long Island Native & Black History, 2008, p. 3.
  4. Gaynell Stone, The Shinnecock Indians: A Culture History, p. 313.
  5. Beverly Jensen, Shinnecock Indian Nation.
why_this_matters: Rev. Paul Cuffee shows Native-led ministry, travel, education, and community continuity across Shinnecock, Unkechaug, Montaukett, and related Long Island Native communities.
